elements.quote: Socio-Economic, Environmental And Demographic Determinants Of Rise In Obesity Among Pakistani Women: A Systematic Review
elements.reason: The title explicitly includes 'A Systematic Review'.

elements.quote: Socio-economic, environmental and demographic determinants of rise in obesity among Pakistani women
elements.reason: The title specifies the population (Pakistani women), exposure (determinants), and outcome (rise in obesity).
The title does not provide supplementary information such as timeframe, analysis method, or study designs, which are relevant based on the review content.

elements.quote: Recent data from both the National Nutrition survey (NNS-2011) and Pakistan Demographic and Health Survey (PDHS2012-13) showed a persistent high prevalence of under-nutrition and anaemia among women coexisting with significant proportion of overweight and obese women. the problem has been underestimated in Pakistan because of scarcity of relevant data and lack of focussed policy in place.
elements.reason: Describes current knowledge on obesity and under-nutrition coexistence and mentions uncertainty due to data scarcity.

elements.quote: This review article was planned to highlight the nutrition transition in Pakistan by exploring the factors contributing to rise in overweight and obesity among women of reproductive age (15-49 years), and possible policy recommendation for policy-makers to deal with this challenge.
elements.reason: Explains the need for the review to address gaps and inform policy.

elements.quote: The current study attempted to investigate the socio-economic, environmental and demographic determinants of rise in obesity among women of reproductive years (15-49 years) in Pakistan.
elements.reason: Explicit statement of review objectives using descriptive framework elements.
The review examines determinants of obesity, not intervention effects.

elements.quote: A limitation of our review is that many lifestyle and dietary patterns of various ethnic groups living in Pakistan were not explored. Both survey reports and relevant data did not have any information on physical activity and energy uptake. We had very few studies that have data on fruit and vegetable consumption. We recommend further research in this area to explore these factors and its association with the emergence of nutrition transition in detail.
